title: Chicken tetrazzini
subtitle: American pasta-and-chicken bake in mushroom cream sauce
excerpt: Thin spaghetti and chunks of cooked chicken baked in a rich mushroom-and-cream sauce, topped with Parmesan and breadcrumbs. Named after opera singer Luisa Tetrazzini; the great American Italian-American pasta casserole.
sourceNotes: Chicken tetrazzini is named after the Italian soprano Luisa Tetrazzini (1871 to 1940), who was enormously popular in American opera circles in the 1900s and 1910s. The dish is believed to have been created in San Francisco (possibly at the Palace Hotel) around 1908 to 1910. It appears in American cookbooks from the 1930s and was one of the signature American-Italian pasta dishes of the twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the breadcrumb topping. Defrost overnight and bake at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to the topping, refrigerate for up to 2 days. Add the topping and bake just before serving.

content.text: Chicken tetrazzini is a casserole in which pasta is the hero. The spaghetti or linguine is baked in a creamy mushroom sauce with chunks of chicken, topped with Parmesan and golden breadcrumbs. It is a crowd-feeding dish: rich, forgiving, and possible to make entirely in advance.

items.prepNote: poached and roughly shredded, or use leftover roast chicken
finely grated; half in the sauce, half on top

content.text: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet time. Drain and set aside. Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).

Melt the butter in a large saucepan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and mushrooms, raise the heat, and cook for 6 minutes until the mushrooms are cooked and the pan is dry. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed. Add the stock and cream, stir, and bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until the sauce is thickened. Stir in half the Parmesan. Season generously.
Add the pasta and chicken to the sauce and toss to combine. Transfer to a large buttered baking dish. Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining Parmesan and scatter over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden on top and bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Pasta was cooked to full doneness before baking
items.fix: Always under-cook the pasta by 2 minutes before baking. It continues to cook in the oven.

content.text: Chicken tetrazzini emerged from Italian-American restaurant culture in early twentieth-century San Francisco and New York. Italian opera stars were cultural celebrities at the time. Naming dishes after them was common practice. The dish crossed into American home cooking by the 1930s. It is now a standard potluck and supper-club dish, made in a large baking dish and brought to gatherings.
